Seurat is an R toolkit for single-cell genomics and supplies a framework in which quality-control workflows can be implemented.
Seurat v5 documents functionality for spatial and multimodal single-cell analysis.
Harmony integrates large and complex single-cell datasets in a corrected embedding space.
RunHarmony requires metadata covariates such as dataset, donor, or batch identifiers to define integration variables.
Scanorama integrates heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq datasets into a low-dimensional representation.
Scanorama can return batch-corrected cell-by-gene expression matrices.
Scanorama documents lowering batch_size as a response to memory pressure during large integrations.
Large Scanorama integrations can encounter memory pressure, for which smaller batches or sketching are documented mitigations.
scvi-tools includes probabilistic models for data integration and dimensionality reduction.
scvi-tools includes models for analysis across single-cell multi-omic data.
Scrublet identifies doublets in single-cell RNA-seq data by simulating doublets and classifying observed transcriptomes.
Scrublet thresholds continuous doublet scores to produce predicted-doublet labels, and the threshold should be reviewed for the observed score distribution.
Scrublet may perform poorly on merged samples whose cell-type proportions do not represent an individual capture.
DoubletFinder predicts doublets in single-cell RNA-seq data using artificial nearest-neighbor structure.
DoubletFinder uses pK selection and an expected-doublet count to threshold pANN-based classifications.
DoubletFinder documentation advises against integrated objects and against merged captures that could create impossible artificial doublets.
scDblFinder detects and handles doublets or multiplets in single-cell sequencing data.
scDblFinder accepts sample identifiers so sample-specific doublet rates can be modeled for multiple captures.
The expected doublet-rate prior strongly affects the scDblFinder classification threshold even when score ranking changes little.
CellTypist assigns cell-type labels to query cells using a selected reference classifier model.
In-memory CellTypist annotation requires log1p-normalized expression in AnnData and checks X before raw.X.
CellTypist annotation returns per-cell predicted labels together with decision and probability matrices.
CellTypist majority_voting optionally refines predictions using over-clustering information.
CellTypist rejects unsuitable normalization and warns that removing genes after normalization may reduce prediction quality.
SingleR annotates single-cell transcriptomes by correlation with reference expression profiles from pure cell types.
The scVI method family is used for probabilistic representation learning and integration of single-cell RNA measurements.
scVelo provides scalable RNA velocity analysis that recovers directed dynamic information from splicing kinetics.
RNA velocity analysis estimates directed cellular dynamics represented by velocity information.
scVelo can infer latent time to reconstruct the temporal sequence of transcriptomic events.
CellRank estimates differentiation direction and maps cellular fates from biological transition priors.
CellRank combines biological priors into Markov transition kernels for fate analysis.
CellRank infers terminal macrostates, fate probabilities, and driver genes.
tradeSeq discovers genes that are differentially expressed along one or multiple lineages.
tradeSeq differential testing is scoped to one or multiple inferred lineages.
tradeSeq provides statistical tests for lineage-associated differential-expression questions.
moscot supports trajectory inference using optimal transport with temporal, spatial, or lineage information.
moscot supports modality translation and other optimal-transport applications across single-cell modalities.
Waddington-OT uses optimal transport to identify developmental trajectories from time-resolved single-cell expression snapshots.
MOFA integrates multi-omic datasets in an unsupervised factor-analysis framework.
MOFA accepts multiple omics matrices measured on the same or overlapping sets of samples.
MOFA infers an interpretable low-dimensional representation composed of latent factors across data modalities.
cell2location maps fine-grained cell types in spatial transcriptomic data by decomposing spatial RNA counts using reference signatures.
cell2location takes spatial transcriptomic count data as one model input.
cell2location requires single-cell-derived reference cell-type expression signatures for spatial mapping.
cell2location estimates cell-type abundance across spatial locations.
MIMOSCA supports perturbation-aware analysis of molecular circuits from pooled single-cell perturbation experiments.
SoupX removes ambient RNA contamination from droplet-based single-cell RNA-sequencing data.
